Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: privacy-policy
Version: 1.0.5

The skill is a straightforward privacy policy template generator. The primary logic in `scripts/privacy.sh` safely parses user-provided arguments (e.g., company name, email) and outputs formatted text for GDPR, CCPA, or standard privacy policies to stdout. There is no evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or prompt injection across the analyzed files.

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent for generating privacy policies: its description, help text, and included shell script align. Before installing or running it, review the full scripts/privacy.sh contents (the provided snippet is truncated) and look specifically for any of the following: network calls or URLs (curl, wget, nc, netcat, scp, rsync, ftp, ssh), commands that send data (curl|wget with POST/PUT), calls that encode or exfiltrate data (base64, openssl used to send data), or writes to sensitive system paths. If you cannot review the full script, execute it in a sandbox or isolated environment, avoid running as root, and run with sample inputs first (or a --help/dry-run) to inspect output. Also consider verifying the source (owner ID, homepage) and, for legal use, have a qualified lawyer review generated policies before publishing.
